threats.title: vLLM image loader passes EPS input to Ghostscript
threats.headline: vLLM image requests can reach host Ghostscript, enabling command execution on vulnerable hosts
threats.summary: The same path also exposes a Pillow denial-of-service issue that can exhaust media-loading workers.
actions: Check whether hosts running vLLM have a vulnerable Ghostscript build installed.

action_quotes.action: Check whether hosts running vLLM have a vulnerable Ghostscript build installed.
action_quotes.quote: Deployments without Ghostscript or with a build fixed for CVE-2024-29510 are not affected by this execution chain.

who: vLLM deployments accepting image input
hosts with vulnerable Ghostscript installed
threats.quote: On a host with Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, this exposes the known Ghostscript sandbox escape through vLLM's image-loading path and can execute commands with the vLLM process's privileges.

threats.title: vLLM shared-memory multimodal cache allows forged pickle loading
threats.headline: Authenticated vLLM callers can run arbitrary Python in workers when SHM multimodal caching is enabled
threats.summary: When vLLM's SHM multimodal cache is enabled, the worker trusts an address and monotonic_id pair supplied in a request to read shared memory. An authenticated caller can forge this pair to point at bytes they staged in the ring buffer, which the worker then passes to pickle.loads(). This works through ordinary public HTTP routes even with insecure serialization disabled, and the proof also made the engine health endpoint fail.
actions: Check whether the SHM multimodal processor cache is enabled.

action_quotes.action: Check whether the SHM multimodal processor cache is enabled.
action_quotes.quote: When --mm-processor-cache-type shm is enabled, vLLM's multimodal SHM cache represents a cached item with an address and monotonic_id pair and treats that pair as authority to dereference shared memory in the worker.

who: vLLM deployments using SHM multimodal caching
multi-tenant vLLM inference services
threats.quote: An ordinary authenticated inference caller can execute arbitrary Python in the worker process on a deployment that uses SHM multimodal caching.

threats.title: TWCA Registration Authority server accessed without authorization
threats.headline: TWCA reports unauthorized access to its Registration Authority server; investigation is ongoing
threats.summary: TWCA reported that its security monitoring detected indicators of unauthorized access to its Registration Authority server. The affected server was isolated and the investigation is ongoing. TWCA states that no certificate mis-issuance has been identified to date and that a full incident report will follow.
threats.quote: TWCA's security monitoring systems detected indicators of unauthorized access to our Registration Authority (RA) server.

threats.title: vLLM Phi-4 multimodal audio encoder memory exhaustion
threats.headline: One legal 10-minute audio clip can crash vLLM engines serving Phi-4-multimodal-instruct
threats.summary: A single 600 second audio clip, within default limits, drove GPU memory up until the engine crashed and the server went down. An unauthenticated client that can reach the chat/completions API could take the service offline until restart.
who: vLLM deployments serving Phi-4-multimodal-instruct
models reusing the Phi-4 audio tower
threats.quote: Full denial of service, requiring a process restart.

threats.title: vLLM DeepSeek-OCR image validation crashes the engine
threats.headline: A single ordinary PNG can permanently crash vLLM servers running DeepSeek-OCR family models
threats.summary: This trips an assertion in the engine worker that is not contained per request, and the whole process tree shuts down. An unauthenticated chat request under default configuration can take the server down until a manual restart.
threats.quote: /health refuses connections until a manual restart.

threats.title: vLLM out-of-vocabulary token id crashes the engine
threats.headline: Pre-tokenized prompts with one out-of-range token id can crash vLLM engines serving Llama-2-family models
threats.summary: vLLM's input validation accepts a token id equal to the vocabulary size for models such as the Llama-2 family, which is one past the last embedding row. At tensor-parallel size 1 the lookup is not masked, so the id triggers a CUDA device-side assert that takes the engine down. Any client able to send pre-tokenized input can trigger it.
who: single-GPU vLLM deployments of Llama-2-family models
services accepting pre-tokenized prompts
threats.quote: At tensor-parallel size 1 the embedding lookup does not mask indices, so the id reaches F.embedding out of range and raises a CUDA device-side assert, which poisons the engine's CUDA context and takes the engine down.

threats.title: vLLM chat template rendering lacks limits, enabling denial of service
threats.headline: One short chat template request can block all chat endpoints for every tenant on a vLLM replica
threats.summary: One authenticated request under 100 bytes can wedge all chat-style endpoints until restart, and a string-multiplication variant kills the API-server process through memory exhaustion. A malicious model repo whose tokenizer config carries a hostile template can do the same to every replica that loads it.
who: multi-tenant vLLM deployments
vLLM servers loading untrusted model repos
threats.quote: In a multi-tenant deployment this is a cross-tenant denial-of-service from any one tenant.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK HTTP transports lack request limits
threats.headline: MCP TypeScript SDK servers over HTTP accepted unlimited bodies and batches, enabling unauthenticated denial of service
threats.summary: MCP servers built with the TypeScript SDK and reachable over HTTP put no limit on POST body size or on the number of messages in a JSON-RPC batch. Large requests could exhaust server memory, and one long batch could block the server from serving anyone else. No credentials were needed unless the application authenticates requests before they reach the SDK.
actions: Cap request body size in a reverse proxy until the SDK is upgraded.

action_quotes.action: Cap request body size in a reverse proxy until the SDK is upgraded.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, cap request body size in a reverse proxy.

who: MCP servers built on the TypeScript SDK
servers reachable over Streamable HTTP by untrusted clients
threats.quote: Large requests could exhaust the server's memory, and one long batch could block it from serving anyone else.

threats.title: vLLM request-controlled processor code revision allows code execution
threats.headline: Untrusted vLLM multimodal requests can swap processor code revision, running arbitrary code on remote-code deployments
threats.summary: Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process.
actions: Keep trust_remote_code disabled where it is not required.
Put the tokenize endpoint behind authentication.

action_quotes.action: Keep trust_remote_code disabled where it is not required.
action_quotes.quote: The default trust_remote_code=False configuration is not affected.

action_quotes.action: Put the tokenize endpoint behind authentication.
action_quotes.quote: Protect /tokenize with the configured authentication policy as defense in depth.

who: vLLM operators with trust_remote_code enabled
deployments serving multimodal models with dynamic processor code
threats.quote: Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process.

threats.title: LiteLLM proxy arbitrary local file read via credentials alias
threats.headline: Low-privilege LiteLLM proxy users could read local files, exposing master and provider API keys
threats.summary: Reading environment files can disclose the master key and provider API keys, escalating to full proxy-admin control.
who: LiteLLM proxy operators
deployments granting internal_user_viewer through SSO
threats.quote: Reading files such as /proc/self/environ can disclose LITELLM_MASTER_KEY and provider API keys, so the impact can escalate to full proxy-admin control.

threats.title: LiteLLM proxy salt key reuse allows admin escalation
threats.headline: LiteLLM internal users could forge admin tokens and run arbitrary commands on the proxy host
threats.summary: An internal user could request an API key with a forged admin credential in its metadata, then present the encrypted result as a bearer token to gain full administrative access. That access includes executing arbitrary commands through the MCP stdio endpoint.
actions: Turn off experimental UI login until patched, accepting that CLI SSO and gateway login break.

action_quotes.action: Turn off experimental UI login until patched, accepting that CLI SSO and gateway login break.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade immediately, set EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=false .

who: LiteLLM proxy operators
deployments with internal_user accounts
threats.quote: An internal user can escalate to proxy admin and execute arbitrary commands on the host.

threats.title: MCP Python SDK accepts bearer tokens for other services
threats.headline: MCP Python SDK servers accepted tokens issued for other services sharing the same authorization server
threats.summary: The MCP Python SDK's server-side bearer authentication had no way to check a token's audience. Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by the MCP server. Patched versions add an opt-in check that stays off unless configured.
actions: Turn on token resource validation after upgrading, since it is off by default.
Reject tokens whose audience does not include your server in the token verifier.

action_quotes.action: Turn on token resource validation after upgrading, since it is off by default.
action_quotes.quote: The patched versions add a validate_token_resource setting that is off unless you set it.

action_quotes.action: Reject tokens whose audience does not include your server in the token verifier.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, reject any token whose aud does not include your server inside verify_token() .

who: MCP servers using the Python SDK bearer authentication
servers sharing an authorization server with other services
threats.quote: Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by your MCP server.

threats.title: MCP Python SDK clients leak headers on cross-origin redirects
threats.headline: MCP Python SDK HTTP clients sent custom credential headers and bodies to any redirect target
threats.summary: Anyone able to make a trusted endpoint redirect elsewhere could capture that material.
actions: Rotate credentials that a client may have sent through a redirect to an untrusted host.

action_quotes.action: Rotate credentials that a client may have sent through a redirect to an untrusted host.
action_quotes.quote: If a client may already have followed a redirect to a host you do not control, rotate the credentials it carried.

who: applications using the MCP Python SDK as an HTTP client
clients sending custom credential headers
threats.quote: Anyone able to make an endpoint you trust redirect elsewhere (a stale redirect to a lapsed domain, a misrouted proxy rule, redirect logic an attacker can influence) could capture that material.

threats.title: MCP Python SDK client fetches server-chosen schema references
threats.headline: Malicious MCP servers could make Python SDK clients fetch URLs, read local files, or freeze
threats.summary: A server could make the client request a URL or read a local file from the client's own network position on every tool call. A target that held the connection open could freeze every session in the client process.
actions: Call tools only on trusted servers until upgraded.

action_quotes.action: Call tools only on trusted servers until upgraded.
action_quotes.quote: Until you can upgrade, call tools only on servers you trust.

who: applications using the MCP Python SDK as a client
clients calling tools on servers they do not control
threats.quote: the fetch ran synchronously on the event loop with no timeout, so a target that accepted the connection and then went quiet froze every session in the process for as long as it held the connection.

threats.title: LiteLLM proxy reflected XSS in SSO debug callback
threats.headline: Unauthenticated LiteLLM SSO debug route allowed script injection leading to proxy admin account takeover
threats.summary: An attacker with an account on the configured identity provider could craft a callback URL and deliver it to a logged-in proxy admin. Scripts running in the proxy origin can read the dashboard session cookie and act with the victim's privileges.
who: LiteLLM proxy admins
deployments using SSO
threats.quote: Scripts executing in the proxy origin can read the dashboard session cookie and act with the victim's privileges, up to full admin account takeover.

threats.title: vLLM multimodal processor kwargs allow out-of-memory denial of service
threats.headline: Unvalidated per-request processor arguments let one request crash shared vLLM servers through memory exhaustion
threats.summary: A remote client can set values such as image size or patch count so that one request exhausts CPU or GPU memory and terminates the shared service process.
actions: Place an authentication layer in front of exposed vLLM API servers.
Allow per-request processor overrides only for trusted clients.

action_quotes.action: Place an authentication layer in front of exposed vLLM API servers.
action_quotes.quote: Authentication: vLLM's API key is optional, so deployments without an external authentication layer are remotely reachable without privileges.

action_quotes.action: Allow per-request processor overrides only for trusted clients.
action_quotes.quote: Operators serving only trusted clients can explicitly opt in to the existing override behavior.

who: operators of vLLM servers serving multimodal models
all users of a shared vLLM service instance
threats.quote: For processors that upscale inputs, a single request can force an allocation large enough to terminate the API server or worker with an out-of-memory condition.

threats.title: uv bundled CA store trusts compromised emSign root
threats.headline: uv's vendored root bundle trusts an emSign root whose intermediate keys are compromised, enabling MITM
threats.summary: uv verifies TLS against a vendored copy of the webpki-root-certs bundle, which in affected versions includes the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root. Eight eMudhra intermediates chaining to that root have compromised private keys. An attacker with one of the keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname and use them for MITM attacks.
threats.quote: An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname, and can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks.

threats.title: Python certifi bundles root behind compromised eMudhra intermediates
threats.headline: certifi trusted an emSign root whose intermediates had compromised keys, exposing requests, urllib3 and pip users
threats.summary: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys.
actions: Rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

action_quotes.action: Rebuild container images that vendor certifi.
action_quotes.quote: Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

who: Python clients using requests, urllib3 or pip
container images that vendor certifi
Python.org macOS installer users
threats.quote: An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname.

threats.title: rustls-webpki may accept compromised emSign intermediates
threats.headline: rustls-webpki could accept certificate paths through emSign intermediates whose private keys are now well known
threats.summary: The private keys for these intermediates are now well known. Fixed versions reject paths containing these public keys.
threats.quote: The private keys corresponding to these intermediates are now well known.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK server memory exhaustion
threats.headline: A single unauthenticated HTTP request can crash MCP TypeScript SDK servers by exhausting memory
threats.summary: One HTTP request within the default 4 MiB size limit could exhaust the server's memory, and the process aborted with JavaScript heap out of memory .
actions: Turn on the new tool input element limit, since upgrading does not enable it.
Reduce the request size limit to what tools need.

action_quotes.action: Turn on the new tool input element limit, since upgrading does not enable it.
action_quotes.quote: Upgrading alone changes nothing.

action_quotes.action: Reduce the request size limit to what tools need.
action_quotes.quote: Lower the request size limit to what your tools need.

who: MCP servers reachable over HTTP by untrusted clients
threats.quote: One HTTP request within the default 4 MiB size limit could exhaust the server's memory, and the process aborted with JavaScript heap out of memory .

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK experimental tasks lack session binding
threats.headline: MCP TypeScript SDK clients sharing a task store could list, read and cancel others' tasks
threats.summary: In affected versions, the experimental tasks feature did not check which session created a task. Clients sharing one InMemoryTaskStore could list, read and cancel each other's tasks. Only HTTP servers that pass taskStore to McpServer or Server are affected.
actions: Stop using the deprecated experimental tasks feature.
Remove the task store or use one per session until upgraded.

action_quotes.action: Stop using the deprecated experimental tasks feature.
action_quotes.quote: The best course of action is to stop using them.

action_quotes.action: Remove the task store or use one per session until upgraded.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, remove taskStore , or create one InMemoryTaskStore per session.

who: MCP HTTP servers using experimental taskStore
threats.quote: Clients sharing one InMemoryTaskStore could list, read and cancel each other's tasks.

threats.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys compromised
threats.headline: Flawed key generation let anyone recover eMudhra intermediate CA keys, exposing TLS clients outside browsers
threats.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were incorrectly generated by the CA, so anyone could recover them from the certificates. Six are for TLS and chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs, and two are for codesigning and trusted by Microsoft. An attacker with any of these keys could impersonate any website or service, and clients that ship their own CA bundle or do not enforce Certificate Transparency are at greater risk.
actions: Update Python certifi to 2026.10.19 or later
Update Claude Code to 2.1.303 or later
Update curl CA bundle to 2026-10-20 or later
Update Docker Engine to 29.9.2 or later
Update applications and libraries that ship their own CA bundle.

action_quotes.action: Update applications and libraries that ship their own CA bundle.
action_quotes.quote: However, many other clients do not consume revocation information and require software updates to ensure they no longer trust the compromised intermediates.

action_quotes.action: Update browsers and operating systems.
action_quotes.quote: Users should update their browsers and operating systems to the latest versions as soon as possible.

who: TLS clients that ship their own CA bundle
command-line tools that do not enforce Certificate Transparency
apps built on Electron
threats.quote: An attacker with the private key of any of the compromised intermediate CAs could impersonate any website or service.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript SDK bearer auth skips audience check
threats.headline: MCP servers using SDK bearer auth accepted tokens issued for other services
threats.summary: Servers are affected if their verifyAccessToken() does not check the token audience itself.
actions: Turn on the new audience setting, since upgrading does not enable it.
Reject tokens whose audience does not include the server.

action_quotes.action: Turn on the new audience setting, since upgrading does not enable it.
action_quotes.quote: Upgrading alone changes nothing.

action_quotes.action: Reject tokens whose audience does not include the server.
action_quotes.quote: If you cannot upgrade yet, reject any token whose aud does not include your server inside verifyAccessToken() .

who: MCP HTTP servers using requireBearerAuth() or verifyBearerToken()
deployments sharing an authorization server across services
threats.quote: Where one authorization server issues tokens for several services, a valid token for another service was also accepted by your MCP server.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript client SDK leaks secrets on redirects
threats.headline: MCP client transports and OAuth requests followed cross-origin redirects, leaking headers, tokens and client secrets
threats.summary: A redirect target received custom headers such as API keys and the mcp-session-id header.
actions: Rotate keys and secrets and revoke tokens if a redirect may have reached an untrusted host.

action_quotes.action: Rotate keys and secrets and revoke tokens if a redirect may have reached an untrusted host.
action_quotes.quote: If a redirect may have reached a host you do not control, rotate the API keys and client_secret your application held and revoke its tokens.

who: apps using StreamableHTTPClientTransport or SSEClientTransport
apps using the SDK OAuth client functions
threats.quote: On a 307 or 308 it also received the request body, including OAuth token requests with their refresh_token and client_secret .
